_aide: English glossary. Same order and fields as glossaire.json; termeFr links each entry to its French term; nomFr is the French name shown with the FR marker. See CLAUDE.md.

termes.definition: SAP's project methodology for S/4HANA, in six phases: Discover, Prepare, Explore, Realize, Deploy, Run.
termes.pourLeDP: The common framework spoken by SAP, integrators and customers. The ACT100 certification is built on it.

termes.definition: Pre-project phase: discover the solution, build the business case and choose the approach.
termes.pourLeDP: This is where greenfield, brownfield or bluefield is decided.

termes.definition: Project kick-off: team, governance, plan, systems, cross-cutting strategies.
termes.pourLeDP: A sloppy Prepare is paid for in Realize: key users, ground rules and the data strategy must be fixed here.

termes.definition: Business needs are confronted with SAP standard (fit-to-standard) and gaps are decided.
termes.pourLeDP: The phase that fixes scope. Gaps badly settled here come back as change requests.

termes.definition: Build in sprints: configuration, development, data migration, testing.
termes.pourLeDP: The longest and most expensive phase; this is where a supplier's OTD is won or lost.

termes.definition: Final preparation and switchover: training, cutover, go / no-go, go-live.
termes.pourLeDP: Everything rides on rehearsing the cutover and on go criteria written in advance.

termes.definition: Operations after go-live: hypercare, then maintenance and continuous improvement.
termes.pourLeDP: The handover to run must be prepared during build, not discovered afterwards.

termes.definition: Workshops where the standard SAP process is shown to the business, who decide whether to adopt it.
termes.pourLeDP: Replaces ASAP's Business Blueprint. Start from the standard and justify every gap.

termes.definition: Former method (ASAP): all requirements were written first, then the solution was designed.
termes.pourLeDP: The equivalent of Explore in the old method, but starting from requirements rather than from the standard.

termes.definition: Formal checkpoint at the end of a SAP Activate phase, with exit criteria.
termes.pourLeDP: A gate passed “with conditions” and no follow-up of those conditions is worthless.

termes.definition: Start from scratch on S/4HANA from the standard, bringing over only the useful data.
termes.pourLeDP: The most transformation, the most change management.

termes.definition: Convert the existing ECC system to S/4HANA, with its configuration, code and history.
termes.pourLeDP: Faster and less risky for the business, but you also keep the bad processes.

termes.definition: Hybrid approach: keep part of the existing system, redesign the rest, and transfer a selection of data.
termes.pourLeDP: The approach that varies most depending on the integrator and the transition tool.

termes.definition: Selective transfer of data to S/4HANA: by company code, by period, with transformations.
termes.pourLeDP: The technical heart of bluefield; requires a tool and scarce experts.

termes.definition: Deployment of a core model already live at other sites or countries.
termes.pourLeDP: Effort concentrates on data, testing, training and cutover, not on design.

termes.definition: The common SAP solution (processes, configuration, developments) subsequently deployed at each site.
termes.pourLeDP: An unstable core model makes every site pay for its fixes.

termes.definition: Assessment of a site's readiness before a roll-out: processes, data, infrastructure, people.
termes.pourLeDP: Your written evidence if the site is not ready and the date slips.

termes.definition: Comparison of the site against the core model, with a decision on each local gap.
termes.pourLeDP: Demand a legal or quantified justification for every local gap.

termes.definition: A requirement that standard SAP does not cover as is.
termes.pourLeDP: Every gap kept costs build, testing and maintenance.

termes.definition: Classification of custom developments: Reports, Interfaces, Conversions, Enhancements, Forms, Workflows.
termes.pourLeDP: Configuration is not part of it. Used to size and track custom work.

termes.definition: Principle: never modify SAP standard; extend only through intended means (extensions, released APIs).
termes.pourLeDP: Makes upgrades fast. The design authority must enforce it.

termes.definition: Body that validates solution choices: compliance with the standard, the core model and Clean Core.
termes.pourLeDP: It says whether something can be done cleanly; the change board says whether we do it.

termes.definition: Body that accepts, rejects or defers any change to scope, schedule or budget.
termes.pourLeDP: Protects you under a fixed-price contract: every change is quantified and billed rather than absorbed.

termes.definition: Formal request for a change, with its impact analysis.
termes.pourLeDP: No CR, no change: the rule that protects your margin.

termes.definition: Executive body that arbitrates, validates gates and decides on go / no-go.
termes.pourLeDP: A committee that observes without deciding lets problems pile up.

termes.definition: Business owner of an end-to-end process; decides and signs off.
termes.pourLeDP: Without them, Explore decisions get challenged later.

termes.definition: Expert business user seconded to the project: workshops, acceptance testing, training colleagues.
termes.pourLeDP: Reserve them in writing. A part-time key user is the first cause of drift.

termes.definition: Business owner of a data object; validates the rules and signs off each migration.
termes.pourLeDP: They sign off; they do not delegate to IT.

termes.definition: Person who maintains data quality day to day, under the data owner's authority.
Table stating for each activity who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed.
termes.pourLeDP: Have it signed between customer, integrator and subcontractors from Prepare.

termes.definition: Justification of the project: expected benefits, costs, risks.
termes.pourLeDP: Quantified objectives are then used to arbitrate.

termes.definition: SAP offer bundling S/4HANA private cloud, hosting and services in a single contract.
termes.pourLeDP: Changes the split of roles: SAP hosts and operates part of the technical stack.

termes.definition: SAP offer for S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, mainly for mid-sized companies and new customers.
Indicators green on the outside, reality red on the inside.
termes.pourLeDP: Countermeasure: quantified alert thresholds and verification on the ground.

termes.definition: Value beyond which you act: “I monitor X; if X exceeds Y, I do Z.”
termes.pourLeDP: The reflex expected of a PD in an interview.

termes.definition: Software that manages purchasing, sales, production, inventory and finance in a single database.
SAP's former ERP. Mainstream maintenance until end of 2027, paid extended maintenance until end of 2030, then the RISE transition option beyond, under conditions.
termes.pourLeDP: The end of maintenance dictates the timeline of many programs.

termes.definition: SAP's new ERP, on the HANA database, with a simplified data model and Fiori.
Purchasing and inventory management module.
Quantity-based stock management: receipts, issues, transfers. Knows how many, not where on the shelf.
Purchasing: purchase requisitions, purchase orders, contracts.
Sales: quotations, sales orders, deliveries, billing.
Production planning and control: production orders, bills of materials, routings.
Quality management: inspections, inspection lots, non-conformances.
Equipment maintenance: maintenance orders, preventive plans.
General ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets.
Management accounting: cost centers, product costing, profitability.
termes.pourLeDP: In S/4HANA, FI and CO share the same table (Universal Journal).

termes.definition: Single S/4HANA table where FI and CO post together.
termes.pourLeDP: End of FI/CO reconciliations; strong impact on finance in a migration.

termes.definition: Single S/4HANA object replacing ECC's separate customer and vendor records.
termes.pourLeDP: Often the critical path of a brownfield (CVI conversion).

termes.definition: Advanced warehouse management: storage bins, tasks, handling units. Replaces LE-WM.
EWM integrated in the S/4HANA system itself.
termes.pourLeDP: Simpler and cheaper: no ERP–warehouse interface.

termes.definition: EWM in a separate system, linked to the ERP through deliveries. Can be connected to ECC or S/4HANA.
termes.pourLeDP: Handles large volumes better and can be migrated independently of the ERP.

termes.definition: ECC's classic warehouse management. In S/4HANA it only exists in the compatibility packs, with limited use (end of May 2026 without a cloud contract, end of 2030 under a cloud contract). Successors: EWM or Stock Room Management.
termes.pourLeDP: A decision to make at scoping: it is often a project within the project.

termes.definition: Multi-currency inventory valuation, mandatory in S/4HANA.
Net requirements calculation: what to buy or make, how much and when, from demand and stock.
termes.pourLeDP: Wrong stock gives a wrong MRP, hence wrong receipts.

termes.definition: S/4HANA version of MRP, much faster thanks to HANA.
Monthly process aligning demand and capacity over 12 to 24 months, by product family.
termes.pourLeDP: In SAP, done in IBP. Its decisions then flow down into MRP.

termes.definition: SAP's cloud planning tool: S&OP, forecasting, inventory.
List of a product's components, with quantities.
Order placed with a supplier.
Order received from a customer.
Shipping notice: the supplier announces what it is sending and when.
Document announcing an expected receipt; the ERP sends it to EWM.
Document requesting that a shipment be prepared; the ERP sends it to EWM.
Posting of a stock receipt.
Posting of a stock issue.
Container tracked in EWM: pallet, case, with its contents.
Quantity of an item produced or received together, tracked for traceability.
Expiry date of an item.
termes.pourLeDP: Must be preserved at all costs in a stock migration.

termes.definition: First in, first out.
SAP's in-memory database, the foundation of S/4HANA.
SAP's modern user interface, made of web apps, on desktop and mobile.
termes.pourLeDP: A visible change for users: plan for it in training.

termes.definition: SAP's cloud platform to build extensions, integrate and analyze, alongside S/4HANA.
termes.pourLeDP: The home of side-by-side extensions, compatible with Clean Core.

termes.definition: SAP's programming language.
Restricted version of ABAP that uses only released APIs, compatible with Clean Core.
Extension point provided by SAP to add behavior without modifying the standard.
Interface that SAP guarantees to keep stable over time.
termes.pourLeDP: Using only these is the foundation of Clean Core.

termes.definition: No-code adaptation by an advanced user: fields, rules, layouts.
Development done on BTP, alongside S/4HANA, communicating through APIs.
Software sitting between systems to carry and translate their messages.
termes.pourLeDP: If it goes down, flows between systems stop: a single point of failure.

termes.definition: SAP's historical middleware. Mainstream maintenance until end of 2027.
termes.pourLeDP: Replacing it with Integration Suite will force interfaces to be migrated and retested.

termes.definition: SAP's cloud middleware on BTP, successor of PI/PO.
In PI/PO, the definition of a flow between two systems: message, direction, synchronous or not.
termes.pourLeDP: A “Service Interface to develop” is an I object in RICEFW.

termes.definition: SAP message format for exchanging data asynchronously between systems.
Real-time SAP technical call from one system to another.
Three-character code identifying a SAP system. The first letter often indicates the environment.
The three environments: development, quality assurance (testing), production.
Package that moves configuration or code from DEV to QAS then PRD.
Carrying production fixes over into the ongoing project, and vice versa.
termes.pourLeDP: A frequent source of regressions: organize it or freeze it.

termes.definition: Technical administration of SAP systems: installation, transports, performance, backups.
Fix or information published by SAP about a known issue.
SAP's lifecycle management tool: requirements, testing, deployments, monitoring.
SAP's AI assistant, embedded in its applications.
Tool that analyzes an ECC system before conversion: simplification items, code, add-ons, volumes.
termes.pourLeDP: First deliverable of a brownfield; to be read item by item.

termes.definition: A change imposed by S/4HANA compared with ECC, documented by SAP.
termes.pourLeDP: Every relevant item must have an owner and a decision.

termes.definition: Automatic code-checking tool, with S/4HANA and Clean Core rules.
SAP tool that runs conversions and upgrades.
SUM option that converts and migrates the database to HANA in a single step.
Copy of a system with its configuration and code but without data, used in bluefield.
Stable data: materials, vendors, customers, bills of materials, accounts.
Data in flight at cutover: undelivered orders, stock, unpaid invoices.
termes.pourLeDP: In greenfield, often the only transactional data carried over.

termes.definition: SAP tool for loading data into S/4HANA.
Full rehearsal of the data load, to measure rejects and duration.
termes.pourLeDP: The first mock must come early; each mock is signed off by the data owner.

termes.definition: Rules that transform a piece of data from the old system into data for the new one.
termes.pourLeDP: To be validated by the business, not by IT alone.

termes.definition: Conversion of ECC customers and vendors into Business Partners.
Moving old data out of the database while keeping it accessible.
termes.pourLeDP: Shortens conversion time in a brownfield.

termes.definition: Comparison of amounts and quantities between the old and new system after a load.
termes.pourLeDP: Mandatory and signed off before opening the system.

termes.definition: Test of an isolated element by the person who built it.
End-to-end tests, interfaces included.
termes.pourLeDP: Exit criteria defined before starting.

termes.definition: Validation of the solution by business users.
termes.pourLeDP: Ends with a signed acceptance record.

termes.definition: Checks that a change has not broken what used to work.
termes.pourLeDP: Essential in roll-out and brownfield; automate it.

termes.definition: Level of seriousness of a defect: blocker, major, minor.
termes.pourLeDP: Decided by the business, not by the delivering team.

termes.definition: Conditions to start and to finish a test phase.
Switch from the old to the new system in production.
Timed list of every cutover task: owner, duration, dependency.
Full, timed rehearsal of the cutover.
termes.pourLeDP: Without a rehearsal, the real cutover overruns its window.

termes.definition: Moment after which you can no longer go back to the old system.
termes.pourLeDP: Fallback criteria are set beforehand.

termes.definition: Plan to return to the old system if the cutover fails.
termes.pourLeDP: A rollback never tested does not work.

termes.definition: Period during which the system is down for the cutover.
Formal decision to switch over or not, on criteria written in advance.
termes.pourLeDP: A no-go is a normal steering option.

termes.definition: Switching everything at once, across all sites and processes.
Switching site by site or country by country.
Period of reinforced support after go-live, with exit criteria.
termes.pourLeDP: Experts leave too early: the classic risk.

termes.definition: Application maintenance entrusted to a run team.
L0: self-service. L1: call center. L2: functional support. L3: experts and developers. L4: SAP, the vendor.
Service-level commitment: response and resolution times.
Run observes the project team, then the reverse (reverse shadowing), before the handover.
Moving to a new version of S/4HANA.
termes.pourLeDP: Quick if Clean Core is respected.

termes.definition: Framework for getting several agile teams to work together on one product.
Group of agile teams delivering together at the same cadence.
Joint planning event for the whole train, every 8 to 12 weeks.
Functionality delivered by the train, broken down into user stories.
termes.pourLeDP: Under a fixed-price contract, the commitment is often taken at feature level.

termes.definition: Share of deliveries made on the promised date.
Share of deliveries that are right first time.
Commitment to a result, at a set price.
termes.pourLeDP: The drift risk sits with the supplier: hence the importance of the change board.

termes.definition: Billing on time spent.
Ready-to-use standard SAP business process with a predefined screen flow and a code (example: BD9 = sales from stock). “Best Practice process” means the same thing.
termes.pourLeDP: Scope is validated scope item by scope item in fit-to-standard workshops.

termes.definition: Smallest unit of Best Practices content: a self-contained, reusable package of settings that makes a scope item work. In Cloud ALM it is called “Business Content”.
termes.pourLeDP: Do not mix them up: the scope item is the recipe, the building blocks are the ingredients.

termes.definition: Standard processes preconfigured by SAP, with their integration and migration content. They exist as documentation (Process Navigator) and as configuration (settings delivered switched off).
The SAP Activate framework rests on three pillars: content (Best Practices), tools (Cloud ALM, Roadmap Viewer…) and methodology (phases, deliverables, tasks, accelerators).
termes.pourLeDP: Exam trap: “Analytics” is not a pillar.

termes.definition: A system whose standard processes work as soon as they are activated, without configuring everything by hand.
termes.pourLeDP: Matters little on an existing core model: the processes are already there.

termes.definition: After the standard is activated, only what differs from the standard is configured. “Delta” means gap.
Methods replaced by SAP Activate: ASAP for on-premise (written blueprint, V-cycle) and SAP Launch for cloud.
TCI: cost of the implementation project. TCO: cost of the system over its whole life, operations included. SAP Activate aims to lower the first, then the second.
termes.pourLeDP: TCO is the central argument against custom code.

termes.definition: Area of work handled by a team that runs across several phases (testing, data, training…). SAP Activate has 11.
termes.pourLeDP: Phases slice the project over time, workstreams slice it by function.

termes.definition: Project Management, Design & Configuration, Extensibility, Integration, Analytics, Testing, Data Management, Technical Architecture & Infrastructure, Customer Team Enablement, Solution Adoption, Operations & Support.
termes.pourLeDP: A reference frame: they can be merged or split. “Training” and “Technical Landscape” do not exist.

termes.definition: A concrete result to produce (example: the cutover plan), attached to a workstream and broken down into tasks.
An action to carry out to produce a deliverable (example: list the cutover steps).
Template or guide provided by SAP and attached to a task, so you do not start from zero (example: a cutover plan template).
Template project plan, phase by phase, with deliverables, tasks and accelerators. Four types: Cloud, On-premise, Upgrade, General.
termes.pourLeDP: “Hybrid” is not a roadmap type. Roadmaps do not list every task: UAT happens even when it is not shown.

termes.definition: SAP Activate roadmap for scenarios involving at least two SAP products: Hire-to-Retire, External Workforce, Source-to-Pay, Total Workforce Management.
Prioritized list of everything still to be built, fed by the gaps found in fit-to-standard.
termes.pourLeDP: Priorities are set by the Product Owner, so by the business, not by the project manager.

termes.definition: Business representative who sets the priority order of the backlog.
Questionnaire that turns business choices into configuration values. Completed in Prepare, it is the basis of the fit-to-standard workshops.
Principle of fit-to-standard workshops: show the process in a system rather than explain it on slides.
Date on which SAP makes a new version available to its customers.
A Clean Core checkpoint in each phase, from QG0 in Prepare to QG5 in Run. SAP analyzes the results and gives recommendations. This is how Clean Core is anchored in the method.
termes.pourLeDP: Applies to RISE customers. Clean Core is therefore not limited to the Run phase.

termes.definition: List of recommended activities, phase by phase, to reach and keep a Clean Core. A tag in the Roadmap Viewer, a template in Cloud ALM.
Governance board that watches over Clean Core and approves every deviation from the standard, based on the 5 Golden Rules.
termes.pourLeDP: The equivalent of a design authority on the customer side; handed over to the operations team at project end.

termes.definition: Digital log, created in Prepare, tracing everything the customer does to respect Clean Core, plus SAP’s recommendations.
termes.pourLeDP: Not to be confused with the cutover runbook.

termes.definition: SAP rules for a cloud ERP: cloud approach (fit-to-standard, agile), preconfigured solutions, modern integration, modern extension (never modify SAP code), deviations made visible.
termes.pourLeDP: Rule 4 forbids modifying SAP code and discourages BAdIs and user exits.

termes.definition: Software Stack & Core, Processes, Extensibility, Integration, Data, Operations: the six axes on which a system is judged “clean”.
termes.pourLeDP: “Reporting”, “Database” and “Operating System” are exam distractors.

termes.definition: SAP’s rules for extensions that survive upgrades.
Accumulated custom code: you save time when you build it, then repay it at every upgrade.
termes.pourLeDP: The argument for a committee: every Z development kept will be retested and fixed at each release, indefinitely.

termes.definition: Customer-specific development whose name starts with Z. Copying a standard program to Z and modifying it is still custom code in the core.
Four steps to deal with an ECC’s custom code: analyze what exists, delete unused code, return to standard, adapt the rest (re-design or re-platform).
termes.pourLeDP: Review starts in Explore, fixes are done in Realize. Keeping the code as is is not an option.

termes.definition: Internal team of SAP experts linking IT and the business and driving continuous improvement. Can rely on an OCC (operations) and an ICC (innovation).

Level 1: Executive Board (funding, vision). Level 2: Steering Committee (approves objectives and changes). Level 3: Operating Committee and Integrating Committee (coordination). Level 4: ongoing meetings.
termes.pourLeDP: Level 1 funds, 2 approves, 3 coordinates, 4 runs the day to day. SAP Activate does not provide for a CCB.

termes.definition: Level-3 body that coordinates all workstreams of a single project and escalates to the Steering Committee.
Level-3 body that ensures consistency across several projects: integration, master data, integration-point register, release strategy.
Workstream that trains the customer’s project team (key users and IT) before the fit-to-standard workshops.
termes.pourLeDP: Not to be confused with Solution Adoption, which trains end users.

termes.definition: Workstream that prepares end users for the change. Three sub-streams: End User Training, Value Management, Organizational Change Management.
Sub-stream of Solution Adoption: identify stakeholders, involve them and have them accept the change, through four analyses (impact, communication, training, stakeholders).
termes.pourLeDP: The OCM impact analysis is done in Explore.

termes.definition: Ambassador of the change within business teams, supported by Train the Trainer.
Internal trainers are trained, then train the end users in turn.
Sub-stream of Solution Adoption that grounds every decision in business value: Business Transformation Reviews at the start, then Value Audits throughout the project.
The PMI’s project management reference, with which the Project Management workstream is aligned.
Contractual document describing the scope of work and usually naming the key governance actors.
Breakdown of the project’s work into packages, with its schedule. An accelerator provided in Prepare.
Official project launch meeting, held in Prepare.
Adoption approach where the different parts of the organization switch one after the other.
termes.pourLeDP: “Big Bang” and “Phased” are adoption approaches; Passthrough and Exhaustive are transition approaches.

termes.definition: Customization approach: the software is used as is, without adaptation (typically multi-tenant cloud).
Software package from the market, adapted to the company’s needs.
Transition approach: go live on the planned date, fix remaining issues afterwards. Fastest value, but very heavy stabilization and strong business involvement.
Transition approach: go live only once all issues are fixed. Risk control, but the latest value.
termes.pourLeDP: Suits risk-averse cultures.

termes.nomComplet: Purely Technical, Leverage Innovations, Embed LoB Products
termes.definition: Three scenarios covered by a single roadmap: follow SAP’s calendar, adopt new functions, integrate products complementary to S/4.
termes.pourLeDP: The heaviest workstream is often Testing, because of regression.

termes.definition: Design principles provided by SAP, read by the team before fit-to-standard workshops (notably for analytics).
Assessment (Excel file) whose results can be loaded into Cloud ALM to define the scope of a public cloud implementation.
A functional area of the company (finance, logistics, HR…).
SAP’s cloud solution for human resources.
SAP’s cloud solution for procurement and supplier relations.
SAP’s cloud solution for managing the external workforce.
SAP’s cloud solution for expenses and travel.
End-to-end HR flow, from hiring to an employee’s departure.
End-to-end purchasing flow, from supplier selection to payment.
Menu that groups all of SAP’s settings in a tree. Opened with transaction code SPRO. Used in on-premise and private cloud.
Transaction code that opens the IMG. The IMG is the menu, SPRO is the shortcut.
S/4HANA screen where Best Practices are activated (a “switchboard”). On-premise it is the customer’s Basis team, in cloud it is SAP.
Simplified configuration screens of the public cloud, replacing the IMG. Public cloud is shared: the customer only gets settings that are safe for updates.
Public cloud tool (hosted on BTP) that presents configuration as a guided task list and creates systems. Milestones: Scope and Configuration.
termes.pourLeDP: Configured with CBC, not SPRO.

termes.definition: SAP website describing standard processes: fact sheets, BPMN2 diagrams, test scripts, setup instructions. It answers “what does the process do?”.
termes.pourLeDP: Full content needs an S-User ID.

termes.definition: SAP website describing the method: deliverables, tasks and downloadable templates, by phase. It answers “how do I run the project?”.
From general to detailed: solution package, scope item group (department or module), business area, scope item (process), building block (settings).
Standard notation for process modeling. Process Navigator diagrams can be downloaded as BPMN2 and edited in Cloud ALM or Signavio.
Personal SAP identifier needed to access many resources (Process Navigator, Business Accelerator Hub…) and open support tickets.
Blogs, Q&A forum, experts and online sessions on SAP Activate.
Suite for process modeling and analysis: Process Insights/Intelligence, Process Manager, Process Governance, Collaboration Hub, Process Explorer. Master tool for processes.
termes.pourLeDP: Not to be confused with Signavio Process Navigator (the Best Practices catalog).

termes.definition: Signavio component that analyzes how processes really run from data: bottlenecks, variants, benchmarks, Z-transaction usage. Also measures template compliance in production (Process Adherence).
Signavio component that gets processes approved: approval flows, version management.
Signavio component that distributes processes to all employees, including training.
Tool mapping the application landscape: applications, owners, links, replacement dates. Master tool for applications, business capabilities and interfaces.
Common vocabulary shared by Signavio, LeanIX and Cloud ALM: a “process” or an “application” means the same thing, and each piece of data is changed only in its master tool.
termes.pourLeDP: Processes: Signavio. Applications: LeanIX. Project, requirements, tests: Cloud ALM.

termes.definition: Classification of processes from the most general (L1, a large domain) to the most detailed (L4, a precise step). The application-to-process link is created in Signavio at L4.
termes.termeFr: Niveaux de processus L1 à L4
termes.nomFr: Niveaux de processus L1 à L4

termes.definition: Set of SAP tools (Signavio, LeanIX, Cloud ALM, Build, Integration Suite) and partner tools (Tricentis, Syniti, WalkMe) exchanging data. Aimed first at Cloud ERP Private (RISE) customers.
Tools to build extensions, automations and AI agents alongside S/4.
Partner test automation tool, used for regression. A partner solution, not a SAP product.
Partner tool for data cleansing and migration. A partner solution, not a SAP product.
Tool that guides the user on screen and measures adoption. Not yet technically linked to Signavio.
Name of a process diagram in Cloud ALM.
Record, kept in LeanIX, documenting an architecture choice: option chosen, justification, applications affected.
LeanIX tool to add non-SAP applications (along with Excel import).
Part of Cloud ALM that monitors the production system: alerts, incident management.
Cloud ALM application opened when a project is created with a roadmap, generating tasks, deliverables and Clean Core Q-Gates.
Historical tool for steering projects and operations, mostly on-premise. Its Focused Build module manages requirements and developments of large agile projects.
termes.pourLeDP: SAP is pushing customers toward Cloud ALM.

termes.definition: Fast access to the latest SAP solutions in the cloud, for example to set up a demo system or deploy a preconfigured system template.
Public cloud: multi-tenant, shared, configured via SSCUI/CBC, New Implementation only. Private cloud: single-tenant, dedicated, configured via IMG/SPRO, New Implementation or conversion.
termes.pourLeDP: “Apartment versus house”. What matters is shared versus dedicated, not who hosts it.

termes.definition: System installed and operated at the customer. The customer manages everything, hardware included.
Multi-tenant: several customers share the same software instance (public cloud). Single-tenant: one dedicated instance per customer (private cloud).
S/4HANA in the cloud, in two versions: Public (shared) and Private (dedicated, sold in RISE with SAP).
Large cloud infrastructure provider (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud) that hosts S/4HANA in RISE.
SAP’s hosting and operations offering. In private cloud some activities (Fiori, SAP Notes, SUM) belong to its team: read the Roles & Responsibilities document.
Prepaid credits to consume BTP services: volume negotiated at sale, monthly statement, annual invoicing in advance, overage billed at list price.
Three sets: Development Efficiency (low-code), Digital Experience (user experience) and Digital Process Automation (workflows and RPA).
Component installed on the customer side that securely links the cloud to the internal network without opening the firewall to inbound connections. Handles HTTP and RFC.
SAP’s cloud integration service, recommended to link two cloud solutions. Process Orchestration is the old on-premise middleware.
Catalog of APIs from SAP and its partners: one-click testing in a sandbox, ready-made integration packages.
Guided configuration of integration scenarios, launched from the Maintenance Planner.
An advanced user adds fields, tables or business rules without a developer. Cloud and on-premise.
Development in ABAP Cloud, a restricted ABAP that survives upgrades. Cloud and on-premise.
Classic ABAP, with full access. Available on-premise only.
termes.pourLeDP: Does not exist in cloud.

termes.definition: Modern interface protocol, used by Fiori and by the standard released APIs.
Classic extension points in SAP code, to be avoided under Clean Core in favor of modern extensions (key user, ABAP Cloud, BTP).
Software extras installed on ECC. The Readiness Check tests their S/4 compatibility: SAP’s are rated, third-party ones are only listed.
Check that verifies how relevant the simplification items are to the system and that data is consistent, before starting the conversion. Each point is fixed or exempted.
SAP tool that calculates the upgrade path and prepares the files to install.
SUM option that adds a move to a new data center to the conversion, for example with a hyperscaler.
Moving a system as is to new infrastructure, without changing version (for example S/4HANA on-premise to private cloud). Uses the Software Provisioning Manager.
termes.pourLeDP: Changes the hosting, not the version.

termes.definition: Parallel copy built on the target database, used by SUM during conversion.

Estimate of the hardware needed. Three methods: user-based (simple, approximate), throughput-based (more precise), customer performance test (most reliable and most costly). Quick Sizer covers the first two.
termes.pourLeDP: A conversion almost always needs new hardware, sized at the start of the project.

termes.definition: Tool that extracts a chosen scope from a source system to transfer it to the target. Ensures consistency and no duplicates. Key tool of Selective Data Transition.
Selective Data Transition that starts from a copy of production emptied of its data, converted to S/4, then loaded with the chosen data.
termes.pourLeDP: Most processes are reused.

termes.definition: Selective Data Transition that starts from a new S/4 (New Implementation) and takes over part of the ECC’s configuration and developments.
termes.pourLeDP: Most processes are redesigned.

termes.definition: Preconfigured public-cloud system (Enterprise Management scope, master data), aligned with the Process Navigator scripts. Fit-to-standard demos run on it.
Public cloud: Quality is configured through CBC after the workshops, Production is updated from Quality by weekly or biweekly transports.
Trial system: in private cloud this is where fit-to-standard demos run; in public cloud, a subscription option to test innovations.
Public cloud subscription service that copies Production data, anonymized, into Quality. Transports only go from Quality to Production.

Already-configured core models adapted to countries, delivered as a fully activated appliance (43 country versions). Successor of SAP Model Company. Does not remove the need for fit-to-standard workshops.
Templates built by partners and validated by SAP, activable in private cloud.
Authorization building blocks of the public cloud. In an upgrade, reviewing them is a critical Realize task; a deprecated catalog disappears two releases later.
Public cloud aid for initial configuration, process testing, data migration and evaluation of activated processes. Does not allow a System Conversion.
Tool built into S/4HANA Cloud whose automated tests reuse the Process Navigator scripts. The Manage Your Test Processes app organizes test plans.
SAP analytics offering (BI, planning, predictive). The portfolio also includes S/4HANA Embedded Analytics, Hybrid Solutions and Analytics Hub.
termes.pourLeDP: Process Orchestration is not part of it: it is an integration tool.

termes.definition: Analytics advisory in three tiers: Baseline (quick diagnosis), Enhanced (roadmap) and Extended (dedicated advisor over time).
Controlling data volume to preserve performance and TCO. Four levers: avoid, summarize, delete, archive.
termes.pourLeDP: Applying DVM in ECC before conversion reduces the volume to migrate. “Data cleansing” is not one of the 4 levers.

termes.definition: Data Management sub-stream that ensures quality, consistent master data.
Data Management sub-stream that takes over data from the old system: master data and a minimum of transactional data.
IT role that manages master data day to day. The Business Data Owner (data custodian), on the business side, is accountable for it.
Test of several elements built in different sprints, to check conformity with the Solution Documentation. Done during the firm-up sprint, in QA.
termes.pourLeDP: Trap: the quiz sometimes gives this definition to UAT.

termes.definition: Checks dependencies between modules and data consistency across the whole solution. Last test run by the project team before UAT.
termes.pourLeDP: Full order: unit, string, integration, UAT.

termes.definition: Checks that roles and authorizations allow each step of the processes to run.
Checks that the system holds the load and stays reliable. In cloud a failure is fixed by adjusting the subscription; on-premise it means buying hardware.
Checks high availability, disaster recovery, backup and restore.
Unit test: the integrator. UAT: the customer’s business. All others (string, integration, regression, security, performance, infrastructure): the customer’s IT.
Sandbox (Prepare, Explore): test strategy. DEV (sprints): unit tests. QA (end of Realize): string, integration, UAT, regression, dress rehearsal. PRD (Deploy): cutover.
termes.pourLeDP: On a new build, regression testing has no value.

termes.definition: Dedicated sprint, at the end of Realize, to test together elements built in different sprints (string test).

termes.terme: Phased vs Big Bang in conversion
termes.definition: A System Conversion transforms a single system: one go-live date, all interfaces switch together. Wave deployment belongs to New Implementation.
termes.pourLeDP: A very frequent exam trap.
termes.termeFr: Phased vs Big Bang en conversion
termes.nomFr: Phased vs Big Bang en conversion

termes.definition: SAP provides 16 operations standards for the Run phase (incident management, change management, monitoring, updates…).
CCoE structure that steers operations.
CCoE structure that steers innovation.

Classification of operations activities in three categories: to create (Fiori server), to modify (backups, monitoring), to remove (monitoring of the old database). Key question: will what the activity manages still exist after go-live?
termes.pourLeDP: S/4 runs only on HANA: monitoring of the old database is to be removed.

termes.definition: The closer to SaaS, the more the provider handles the technical layers (server, OS, database, application). On-premise, the customer manages everything. Even in SaaS, the customer keeps part of operations, including business process management.
Support: software error or defect, wrong documentation, problem with a SAP fix. Consulting: help with configuration, customization request, “how do I…?” question.
termes.pourLeDP: A classic exam trap.

termes.definition: Single entry point to SAP support: licenses, subscriptions, users, announcements, global search and ticket creation through Get Support.
Central contact point for all SAP customers, cloud and on-premise, reachable 24/7, for non-technical topics: licenses, system creation, S-users.

termes.nomComplet: Expert Chat, Schedule an Expert, Ask an Expert Peer, Schedule a Manager
termes.definition: Expert Chat: free chat with support. Schedule an Expert: free appointment. Ask an Expert Peer: external expert validated by SAP, “how do I…?” questions. Schedule a Manager: 15 min, non-technical topic, medium or high priority tickets.
Support AI tool that helps solve a problem in real time or reach an expert. Others: Guided Answers, Support Assistant, Support Log Assistant, Incident Solution Matching.
Application that lets partner consultants open tickets on behalf of the customer with their own S-user: the customer no longer has to create one for them.
SAP support contract that includes Cloud ALM and access to Tricentis Test Automation for SAP.
Leaving hypercare does not mean no bugs remain: it means the criteria are met and operations accepts the remaining issues. A condition to leave Deploy.
Short build cycle in Realize, 2 to 4 weeks, closed by a business demo.
termes.pourLeDP: Activate vocabulary: not to be confused with SAFe terminology.

termes.definition: A set of several sprints (1 to 3 months), closed by a walkthrough with the business. Roughly the equivalent of a PI in SAFe.
A set of waves ending in a go-live. A project can have several releases.
termes.pourLeDP: According to the official diagram, release 2 starts after the hypercare of release 1.

termes.definition: Meeting where each Scrum team sends a representative to handle topics involving several teams.
Short daily team check-in, planned for Realize from Explore.
Large functional set grouping several user stories. Can serve as a fixed-price unit in an agile framework contract.

termes.nomComplet: Fixed price + T&M, bonus, per phase
termes.definition: Five combinations: fixed price plus T&M for custom work; fixed price plus business KPI bonus; fixed price plus success-criteria bonus; one fixed price per phase; empty framework contract plus one fixed price per release, epic or sprint (suited to agile).
Single S/4HANA table where all stock movements are written. It replaces ECC's header and item tables and its stock aggregate tables.
termes.pourLeDP: Custom code that wrote to the old tables must be reworked: measure it during scoping.

termes.definition: ECC functions still shipped in S/4HANA for a limited time. The right to use them expires on a set date: end of May 2026 without a cloud contract, end of 2030 under a cloud contract.
termes.pourLeDP: A reprieve, not a target: put the exit and its budget in the plan.

termes.definition: Simplified carry-over of LE-WM into S/4HANA (since release 1909), with the same data model and fewer functions.
termes.pourLeDP: Shortest route for a simple warehouse; check early that the functions in use exist.

termes.definition: Paid ECC maintenance after mainstream maintenance ends: from 2028 to end of 2030, with no new features.
termes.pourLeDP: Each year of delay costs this extra fee: put it in the business case.

termes.nomComplet: SAP ERP, private edition, transition option
termes.definition: RISE subscription that extends an ECC beyond 2030 (to 2033, and to 2035 under conditions since October 2026). Reserved for systems moved to private cloud before end of 2030.
termes.pourLeDP: Not a postponement for everyone: strict conditions and a higher price.

termes.definition: What the company can promise a customer for a given date, based on stock and planned receipts.
termes.pourLeDP: A promised date without an availability check drives OTD down.

termes.definition: S/4HANA availability check: confirms orders in batches, with allocation and customer priority rules.
termes.pourLeDP: Priority rules are a business decision to be approved.

termes.definition: S/4HANA customer credit management. It replaces ECC credit management: score, limits, credit file per Business Partner.
termes.pourLeDP: A full functional workstream; a badly set block stops shipments.

termes.definition: S/4HANA tool managing customer and supplier rebates through condition contracts. It replaces ECC rebate agreements.
termes.pourLeDP: Settle open agreements before cutover.

termes.definition: S/4HANA mechanism deciding which documents to print or send (invoices, delivery notes), through BRF+ rules. It succeeds ECC's message system (NAST).
termes.pourLeDP: Count the forms at scoping: each one must be retested.

termes.definition: Clearing account between receipt of goods and arrival of their invoice.
termes.pourLeDP: Clean it before cutover, or old differences migrate.

termes.definition: SAP reference listing each product's releases and maintenance dates.
termes.pourLeDP: The source to quote for any end-of-maintenance date.
